resources.string: HowYouDoin joins your WhatsApp as a linked device, just like WhatsApp Web. Your phone stays the main device and you can unlink it at any time.
In WhatsApp, open Settings (on Android: ⋮ menu → Settings) and tap Linked devices.
WhatsApp may ask for your fingerprint, face or PIN to confirm it's you.
WhatsApp opens the camera, but you can't scan your own screen. Tap “Link with phone number instead” at the bottom.
HowYouDoin shows you a code like 1CDB-N2DG. Copy it, switch to WhatsApp and type or paste it.
If HowYouDoin is open on a tablet or computer, point WhatsApp's camera at the QR code it shows.
How do you want to connect?
Connect your chat accounts. They connect directly from this phone; a server bridge is optional.

HowYouDoin is unofficial. WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram, Signal and Slack don't allow third-party apps and may limit or permanently ban an account that uses one. The developer can't restore it, so don't connect an account you can't afford to lose.\n\nThe app is provided "as is", without warranty, and may miss or delay messages. You use it at your own risk.
Your end-to-end encrypted Messenger chats only show new messages. To bring back their history, enter the PIN you set in Messenger, not your phone's or this app's PIN.
The 6-digit PIN you set in Messenger for end-to-end encrypted chats. It's not your phone's PIN, HowYouDoin's app lock PIN or your Facebook password.
Connect from your phone, without the server bridge.

Scan a code with Telegram; needs this code on a second screen.
Link this app as a Signal device by scanning a QR code; the code has to be on a different screen from the phone with Signal.
Link this app as a WhatsApp device directly, without the server bridge.
Same, but type a code on your phone instead of scanning.
Sign in with your Matrix ID and password (matrix.org or your own homeserver).
Sign in to your workspace on slack.com; it connects from this phone.
How do you want to log in?
In WhatsApp, open Settings → Linked devices → Link a device, then tap "Link with phone number instead" and enter or paste this code.
Enter the 6-digit PIN you set in Messenger for end-to-end encrypted chats. It unlocks your saved message history so older encrypted messages appear here too.
Messenger allows only a limited number of wrong attempts. If you're not sure of your PIN, skip this; new messages arrive either way.
Enter the phone number of your Telegram account. Telegram sends you a login code.

In Signal open Settings → Linked devices → Link a new device, and scan this code. Signal's scanner uses the camera, so it needs this code on a different screen than the phone it runs on.

In Telegram open Settings → Devices → Link Desktop Device, and scan this code. Telegram's scanner needs the code on another screen: if Telegram is only on this phone, go back and log in with your phone number instead.
On your phone open WhatsApp → Linked devices → Link a device → Link with phone number instead, and enter this code.

%1$s is reached through a mautrix bridge running next to your homeserver. Enter the public URL where its provisioning API (/_matrix/provision) is served.
HowYouDoin is an unofficial app, not made or supported by Telegram. It uses Telegram's public API, which Telegram allows other apps to use.
Matrix is an open standard: HowYouDoin is one of many apps that work with any Matrix homeserver.
HowYouDoin is an unofficial app, not made or supported by %1$s. %1$s doesn't officially allow other apps, so it could limit an account that uses one.
Enter the number of your %1$s account. You'll get a code to type into %1$s on your phone, under Linked devices.
Your %1$s chats will show up in the inbox over the next few minutes.
Tip: open Messenger on your phone once so it recognises HowYouDoin as one of your devices. Until then, encrypted messages sent from that phone may not arrive here.

1. Enter the email you use for Slack. Slack emails you a code; type it here.\n2. If Slack asks, pick your workspace. When it offers the Slack app, stay in the browser.\nHowYouDoin continues by itself once the workspace opens. Pinch to zoom if the page looks small.

1. Enter your %1$s email or phone number and password, then tap Log in.\n2. If it then shows "Continue as <your name>", tap it. Finish any "confirm it's you" steps here too.\nHowYouDoin continues by itself once you're in. Pinch to zoom if the page looks small.
Its chats, photos and encryption keys are deleted from this phone. Your %1$s account and its messages stay as they are; you can connect again anytime.
